editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 1, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: openclaw/openclaw is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: openclaw/openclaw leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: openclaw/openclaw — 108 commits today, 448.9 below its current daily pace, with 153 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openai/codex — 31 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
unslothai/unsloth — No same-day commit after 570 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Check registration before retrying a Pi MCP sign-in
dailyInsight.insight: Pi has added a configurable OAuth client name for MCP servers. The name is sent when registering a client; changing it does not rewrite an existing registration.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The September 30 source change passes oauth.clientName into dynamic registration metadata and otherwise keeps Pi as the default. Its documentation says a new name requires signing out and registering again.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A rejected registration and a failed tool call are different failures. Checking the registered client identity can explain why a connection never reaches tool discovery.

actions.audience: Pi users testing an MCP server that rejects registration
actions.label: Inspect a disposable registration
actions.instruction: In an isolated configuration using a pinned revision that includes this change, inspect the registration request against a test server you control. Use its documented client name and compare the stored registration with a fresh one. Keep the working account and configuration intact.

receipts.title: Allow a custom OAuth client name for MCP servers
receipts.supports: Adds clientName to registration metadata and leaves the default name unchanged.

receipts.title: Registration-time behavior in the changed documentation
receipts.supports: Explains that the name is sent only during registration and changing it requires registering again.

confidence.basis: The merged OAuth implementation and its versioned documentation agree on when the client name is sent.

dailyInsight.limitation: We inspected source, not a live OAuth integration or an installed release. A configurable client name does not establish provider approval, authorization or successful access.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A pinned reproduction showing the configured name absent from a fresh registration request would contradict this implementation reading.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A public integration receipt identifying the Pi version, accepted registration and successful tool discovery.
